about: A PROJECT-DEFINED EDITORIAL EQUIVALENT, NOT AN EXTERNAL SYLLABUS. NOTHING IN THIS FILE MAY BE ATTRIBUTED TO THE MAHARASHTRA DIRECTORATE OF LANGUAGES OR TO ANY OTHER BODY, AND NOTHING IN IT MAY BE ATTRIBUTED TO DELE, THE INSTITUTO CERVANTES OR THE PLAN CURRICULAR ABOUT MARATHI. No awarding body publishes an A1 Marathi syllabus to restate: core/exam-levels.json records this track as exam 'no widely-sat ladder', basis 'editorial'. The Maharashtra Directorate of Languages does administer lower- and higher-level Marathi examinations for government employees, and marathi/assessment-spec.md already declines to borrow that name; those are role-specific tests, not a public four-skill pre-A1-to-C2 ladder, and no content syllabus, grammar inventory, word list or can-do descriptor set is published for them. THE SEARCH IS SETTLED, DO NOT REPEAT IT: the parallel Hindi effort established the same negative result against the best-placed South Asian candidate -- DBHPS publishes examination names and prescribed readers and no syllabus, Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and the Central Hindi Training Institute publish none, and the Council of Europe has issued no Reference Level Description for Hindi. There is no South Asian equivalent of the Plan Curricular. WHAT THIS FILE DOES INSTEAD IS BORROW A LEVEL, NOT A LANGUAGE. Spanish is the one track here whose A1 point set restates a real awarding body's published inventory, so core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json's 273 points are an attributable statement of what an A1 learner must be able to handle. This file walks them and asks, of each, what it DEMANDS of a learner rather than what Spanish grammar it names -- 'give personal information: name, age, origin' and 'negate a statement' are language-neutral demands, while a point about Spanish gendered articles is not, and its Marathi counterpart is whatever carries the same load. Every point records its origin in `derivedFrom`, so the derivation is auditable line by line rather than gestured at; a point with an empty `derivedFrom` and `marathiSpecific: true` has no Spanish source at all, and `notTransferred` lists the Spanish points that were deliberately dropped and why. A proxy is a scaffold, not a template to translate: Devanagari orthography, the postposition system, the ergative and the gender-marked present have no Spanish counterpart and are here on their own merits. Every point also carries `anchorIds` into the `anchors` array, and every anchor declares a KIND a reader should check before the point. `sourced-proxy` is the Spanish set. `external-framework` is the CEFR Companion Volume -- public, language-neutral, able to anchor a function and never a Marathi form. `project-owned` are files in this repository, finite and auditable but our own work, so agreeing with them is not corroboration. `editorial` is unaided judgement, and an editorial point is a working default to be corrected. The pre-A1/A1 boundary is deliberately NOT what this file is shaped around. The owner's criterion is that a learner finishing the A1 material can sit the A1 paper, and level labels are freely adjustable, so a word or a rule appears here if the A1 papers demand it, whatever rung the curriculum eventually files it under. Finally, read the score as a FLOOR, not an estimate. Coverage is computed from DECLARED atoms, and the track has two bands of lessons that teach real material and declare none: 26 schema-v1 lessons in chapters 9 to 12, and four schema-v2 lessons carrying `introduces: []`. Points affected are marked MEASUREMENT GAP in their notes; they are taught, they are unmeasurable, and they are far cheaper to close than the content gaps they sit beside.
source: PROJECT-DEFINED. LEVEL PROXY: code/learning/human-languages/core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json, the DELE/PCIC-sourced Spanish A1 point set, used for the STRUCTURE of what an A1 learner must handle. Nothing about Marathi is attributed to DELE, the Instituto Cervantes or the Plan Curricular. EXAM ENVELOPE: code/learning/human-languages/marathi/assessment-spec.md#a1 and code/learning/human-languages/marathi/task-shapes/a1.json, which fix the four-skill A1 papers this book must prepare a book-only learner to pass. PROFICIENCY BACKBONE: Council of Europe, CEFR Companion Volume (2020), https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/cefr-companion-volume-and-its-language-versions -- which the Council of Europe states it does not itself validate any examination against. There is no external Marathi A1 syllabus; see core/exam-levels.json, tracks.marathi. NOTE ON METHOD: the parallel Hindi inventory was built by mining that track's checked-in timed MOCKS, because every mock stimulus is a construction a candidate must handle, written down before the inventory and without it in view. Marathi has no mocks -- marathi/assessment.json names mocks/a1/* as required future artifacts and none exist -- so the evidence used here is the Spanish proxy above together with the eleven paper parts of task-shapes/a1.json. Per-point provenance is in `anchors`, `anchorIds` and `derivedFrom`.

anchors.title: core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json -- the DELE/PCIC-sourced Spanish A1 point set, used as a LEVEL proxy
anchors.note: The strongest anchor in this file and the one that needs the most care. Spanish is the only track in this repository whose A1 point set restates a real awarding body's published inventory, so its 273 points are an ATTRIBUTABLE statement about what an A1 learner must handle. This file walks them and asks what each DEMANDS of a learner -- 'give personal information: name, age, origin', 'negate a statement', 'ask a price' -- and writes the Marathi point that carries the same load. WHAT IS BORROWED IS THE LEVEL, NOT THE LANGUAGE: every Marathi exponent named here is this project's editorial judgement, and NOTHING IN THIS FILE MAY BE ATTRIBUTED TO DELE, TO THE INSTITUTO CERVANTES, OR TO THE PLAN CURRICULAR ABOUT MARATHI. Each point records its origin in `derivedFrom`; a point with an empty `derivedFrom` and `marathiSpecific: true` has no Spanish source and rests on the editorial anchors instead.

anchors.title: Council of Europe, Common European Framework of Reference -- Companion Volume (2020)
anchors.note: Public and language-neutral. It describes what an A1 user can DO; it names no Marathi word, letter or ending, and the Council of Europe explicitly does not validate any examination's claimed link to it. It is the backbone the proxy sits on rather than a per-point source.

anchors.title: The shared curriculum spine
anchors.note: Twelve pre-A1 and A1 nodes, each a can-do statement with a finite concept list, shared by all 23 tracks. Cited where a point restates a node, so the boundary is the spine's rather than ours.

anchors.title: Coding Adventures Marathi Assessment specification and contract
anchors.note: The project-defined equivalent this book must prepare a book-only learner to pass. Fixes the assessed variety (contemporary standard Marathi in Devanagari), the four independent 60/100 papers, and the A1 level envelope.

anchors.title: Marathi A1 four-skill task-shape inventory
anchors.note: Finite and already checked in: it names the genres, item counts, stimulus lengths and response modes of every A1 part. A point anchored here is anchored to something a candidate will literally be handed, and it is what settles whether a demand the Spanish set raises really applies to this book's own exam.

anchors.title: Shared assessment policy
anchors.note: Owns the writing-stage ladder and the pass-evidence rules. The stages are deliberately NOT enumerated as points here -- see scope['phonology-orthography'].

anchors.title: CEFR-to-exam mapping ledger
anchors.note: Records Marathi as exam: 'no widely-sat ladder', basis: 'editorial'. This file is the reason the inventory has to be project-defined, and citing it keeps that visible rather than buried.

anchors.title: This project's judgement about which Marathi structures carry a Spanish A1 demand
anchors.note: The structures named -- three genders, the oblique stem, the -laa dative of the experiencer, the -chaa genitive agreeing with the possessed noun, the gender-marked present, the ergative -ne of the past transitive -- are as standard descriptive grammars of Marathi describe them (Berntsen and Nimbkar, A Marathi Reference Grammar; Pandharipande, Marathi, Routledge Descriptive Grammars). Those works describe the structures; they do NOT assign CEFR levels. Deciding that a given Marathi structure is the one carrying a Spanish A1 point's load is this project's own judgement, and a working default to be corrected.

anchors.title: This project's judgement about which everyday domains carry a Spanish A1 demand
anchors.note: The Spanish set closes the DOMAIN list for us -- twenty thematic areas, published -- so what is editorial here is narrower than it would otherwise be: which Marathi words sit in each domain, and whether the corpus holds enough of one to answer an item. A domain point is covered only when the corpus could support an item of the kind the papers set, which is a lower bar than command of the domain and is stated so nobody reads it as the higher one.

proxy.borrowed: the structure of what an A1 learner must handle, point by point
proxy.notBorrowed: any statement about Marathi. Every Marathi exponent is this project's editorial judgement.

notTransferred.why: Marathi has no article system, so the definite article, the indefinite article and the al/del contractions have no counterpart. The DEMAND behind the fourth Spanish article point -- knowing that a bare noun can be definite or indefinite -- does transfer, as MR-A1-DET-01.
Devanagari is unicase. Capital and initial lower-case letters are not a distinction the script makes.

Devanagari writes no stress accent and has no diacritic tilde, so the two written-accentuation points have nothing to land on. Marathi's own stress demand is MR-A1-SN-08, which is a listening point rather than an orthographic one.

communicative-functions.source: core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json (DELE/PCIC-sourced) used as a level proxy; core/spine.d; marathi/task-shapes/a1.json; CEFR Companion Volume (2020) A1 descriptors
communicative-functions.note: MUCH BETTER SOURCED THAN IT WAS, AND STILL NOT CLOSED. The 54 functional points here are derived one by one from the Spanish set's six macro-functions, which are themselves a restatement of a published inventory -- so the BOUNDARY is now borrowed from a real awarding body instead of invented, and the count moved from 24 editorially-chosen functions to 43 proxy-derived ones plus the Marathi-specific remainder. What keeps it partial is that the borrowing is a judgement at every step: a Spanish function transfers only if this project decides the Marathi A1 papers demand it too. Closing this dimension needs either a Marathi source that does not exist, or a reviewed project decision recording that the Spanish functional boundary is accepted wholesale for Marathi.

grammar.source: core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json used as a level proxy; EDITORIAL for every Marathi exponent, informed by standard descriptive grammars (Berntsen and Nimbkar, A Marathi Reference Grammar; Pandharipande, Marathi, Routledge Descriptive Grammars)
grammar.note: The dimension the proxy improved most and the one still to distrust first. Walking the Spanish grammar categories in order -- noun, adjective, article, demonstrative, possessive, quantifier, pronoun, adverb, verb, and the phrase and clause levels -- surfaced whole areas the descriptor route had missed entirely: the demonstratives, the relative clause, coordination, subordination, object marking, and the exclamative. What stays editorial is the mapping: deciding that Marathi's oblique stem carries the load of Spanish's prepositional system, or that the ergative belongs at A1 because the past tense does, is this project's judgement and nobody else's. Three Spanish article points and two accentuation points were dropped as inapplicable and are listed in `notTransferred` rather than silently omitted.

phonology-orthography.source: core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json orthography inventory used as a level proxy; marathi/assessment-spec.md (assessed variety: contemporary standard Marathi in Devanagari); marathi/pronunciation-reference.md
phonology-orthography.note: TWO HALVES WITH DIFFERENT PROVENANCE. The ORTHOGRAPHY half now follows the Spanish orthographic inventory's own structure -- letters, vowel signs, spelling, punctuation, abbreviations and symbols -- which is what surfaced the punctuation and symbol points a Devanagari-first reading had skipped, and it is close to closed because Devanagari as Marathi writes it is a finite inventory. The PHONOLOGY half has no proxy at all: the Spanish file deliberately enumerates NO pronunciation points, because its source publishes the pronunciation band as one undivided A1-A2 block. So the eight sound-system points are wholly editorial, derived from the assessed variety and the 90-110 wpm listening envelope, and that alone keeps this dimension partial. Note one deliberate ABSENCE: the writing-stage ladder is owned by core/assessment-policy.json and measured by the plan's `writing-stage` family; restating it here would double-count the same debt in two queues.

lexicon.source: core/exam-inventory-es-a1.json general and specific notions (DELE/PCIC-sourced) used as a level proxy; core/spine.d LEXICON nodes
lexicon.note: THE DIMENSION THE PROXY CHANGED MOST, AND THE CHANGE IS THE HEADLINE. The Spanish source publishes a closed list of seven general-notion classes and twenty thematic areas, every entry marked A1 or A2. Walking it added the domains an editorially-chosen list had simply never thought of -- education, work, leisure, media, housing, services, shopping, health, travel, money, government, the arts, religion and the natural world -- and the corpus covers almost none of them. That is not the proxy being unfair; it is what an external boundary is FOR. These points still bound DOMAINS rather than words, so the count here is not a count of words: the project's own A1 target is 600 headwords against roughly 50 today, and this dimension names WHICH 600 and in what order the papers ask for them. It stays partial because no ranked A1 Marathi headword list exists to close it, and because deciding which Marathi words populate a Spanish-sourced domain is editorial throughout.

probeSemantics: A point counts as COVERED when every atom in `probe` is introduced by some lesson in the track. `probe: null` means no atom in the corpus corresponds to this point, which is itself the finding -- an unmapped point is uncovered, never skipped, and every null here carries a `note` saying what is missing. Every atom named in a probe EXISTS in the Marathi corpus today, and that rule is enforced both by the generator that wrote this file and by a test. A guessed id -- an atom somebody expects a future lesson to introduce -- resolves to 'not introduced', which is silent, permanent and indistinguishable from real content debt, and would never flip to covered if the author picked a different suffix. So a point whose demonstration would need an atom nobody has written yet gets `null` and a note, not a hopeful probe. ONE MORE DISTINCTION, WHICH THIS TRACK FORCED. A probe reads DECLARED atoms, so a null means one of two quite different things and the note always says which: a CONTENT gap (nobody has taught it) or a MEASUREMENT GAP (it is taught and cannot be measured). Grep for MEASUREMENT GAP to find them. There are two kinds. SCHEMA-V1 MEASUREMENT GAP: 26 of Marathi's 205 lessons, the whole of chapters 9 to 12, are schema-v1 and declare no atoms while teaching mii, tuu/tumhii, maazhaM, kaay, kasaa, 'tumchaM naav kaay aahe?', 'tumhii kase aahaat?', kaam karne and raahne. EMPTY-INTRODUCES MEASUREMENT GAP is worse, because it hides inside schema-v2 where everything looks declared: 66 v2 lessons carry `introduces: []`, most of them honest retrieval lessons that should introduce nothing, but MR-R22-request-verbs and MR-R23-wellbeing-verbs drill five polite imperatives and a future while declaring only the INFINITIVE atoms they review, and MR-A1M17/18 teach the guided and independent 30-to-40-word message -- the A1 writing paper's second task -- while declaring nothing at all. Reading a measurement gap as a content gap would send an author to rewrite chapters 9 and 24.

points.label: proper nouns: personal names, forms of address, place names
common nouns naming periods of time
points.note: No atom names a period of time. SPINE-TIME-OF-DAY is an A1 core node and the track omits all nine of its concepts.

points.label: gender: three genders, inherent and unpredictable from meaning
gender by heteronymy in kinship terms
number: masculine plural formation
points.note: No atom introduces any plural at all. Spanish closes its whole plural system in one point; Marathi needs three, because the classes do not derive from one another.

points.label: number: feminine plural formation
points.note: Untaught. Feminine nouns split into several plural classes and knowing one gives none of the others.

points.label: number: neuter plural formation
points.note: Untaught, and it is the gender the track teaches MOST -- kutumb, khaane, paani are all neuter -- so the gap sits directly on the taught vocabulary.

points.label: the -ne verbal noun: an infinitive that is also a neuter noun
the oblique stem a noun takes before any postposition
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC AND THE LARGEST STRUCTURAL GAP IN THE TRACK. Spanish has no counterpart because it marks case with prepositions and no stem change. Marathi puts almost every case relation on a postposition and almost every postposition demands an oblique stem first, so this one rule stands between the taught vocabulary and any sentence about place, time, direction or accompaniment.

points.label: qualifying adjectives in attributive and predicative use
points.note: SPINE-DESCRIBE-QUALITIES is an A1 core node with no realization in this track at all, so neither use is reachable.

points.label: relational adjectives: naming a language and a people
adjective gender: the -aa class agrees, in three genders rather than two
adjective number and agreement in the plural
points.note: Blocked behind the plurals themselves (MR-A1-N-05 to -07).

points.label: position: prenominal, which is the opposite of the Spanish default
points.note: Never stated. Every taught example happens to be prenominal, so the rule has been demonstrated and never named -- which is exactly the case a reader cannot generalize from.

points.label: degree: khuup and the intensifying reduplication
points.note: Untaught. Spanish's absolute superlative in muy is the same demand: making an adjective stronger.

points.label: invariable adjectives, which do not agree at all
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC contrast with MR-A1-ADJ-03: a learner who has only met agreeing adjectives over-applies the endings. Spanish's -e and consonant-final adjectives are the nearest analogue and are not an A1 point there.

points.label: how a specific known thing is marked when it is marked at all: Marathi has no article
points.note: SPINE-DEFINITE-REFERENCE is an A1 spine node and the track omits its only concept, GRAMMAR-THE. The Spanish points on the definite and indefinite articles and their contractions do not transfer -- Marathi has no article system -- but the DEMAND behind the bare-noun point does: a reader must know that a bare Marathi noun can be either definite or indefinite and that context decides.

points.label: the forms haa/hii/he and to/tii/te, in all three genders
points.note: Untaught, and the reading paper's person-to-detail matching is built on pointing at things.

points.label: spatial deixis: Marathi's two-way near/far against Spanish's three-way
points.note: Untaught. The point transfers with its cardinality changed, which is what a proxy is for.

points.label: position: prenominal, and compatible with a following noun
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: possessives with one possessor: maazaa, tuzaa, tyaachaa
points.note: PART MEASUREMENT GAP (SCHEMA-V1), PART REAL. maazhaM is taught in its own right by MR-C02-majhe (chapter 9, schema-v1, declaring no atom) and appears inside the v2 lines MR-A1-MESSAGE-LINE-NAME and -WRITE-NAME. The PARADIGM is what no lesson supplies: the learner meets one neuter form and cannot change the possessor.

points.label: possessives with several possessors: aamchaa, tumchaa
points.note: tumchaM occurs inside the schema-v1 phrase MR-C02-tumche-naav-kaay-aahe and is introduced nowhere.

points.label: distribution: the genitive agrees with the thing possessed, not the possessor
cardinal numerals six to twenty
points.note: Untaught. Marathi's teens are irregular enough to be learned rather than derived, so one-to-five does not extend by itself.

points.label: cardinal numerals to one hundred: a price, an age, a house number
points.note: Untaught, and demanded three times over by the A1 envelope -- the practical form, the role-play, and the interview's how-old-are-you.

points.label: ordinal numerals to tenth
points.note: Untaught; needed to read a floor number or a date on a notice.

points.label: thodaa and khuup, and their agreement
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: sufficiency: puresaa, baraach
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: subject pronouns: the full paradigm
points.note: SCHEMA-V1 MEASUREMENT GAP, PARTLY. mii and tuu/tumhii ARE taught -- MR-C03-mi (chapter 10) and MR-C02-tu-tumhi (chapter 9) -- but both lessons are schema-v1 and declare no atoms, so nothing can be probed and the point scores zero. Do not send an author to write them again. Genuinely absent are the third person and the plural: to, tii, te and aamhii occur nowhere, which is what the reading paper's person-to-detail part asks for.

points.label: object pronouns: the dative-accusative malaa, tulaa, tyaalaa
points.note: Untaught as a paradigm. malaa appears inside taught lines and the review lesson MR-R25-dative-frame, always with a fixed first person.

points.label: the dative experiencer that the liking verb requires
the reflexive and the inclusive: swatah and aapan
points.note: Untaught. Listed because aapan is the ordinary polite 'you' across much of Maharashtra, so a candidate meets it in the listening paper whether or not the book taught it.

points.label: the relative jo/jii/je with its correlative
points.note: Untaught. Marathi's relative is correlative rather than post-nominal, so the Spanish point transfers as a demand and not as a shape.

points.label: interrogative pronouns: kon, kaay, kitii
points.note: PART MEASUREMENT GAP (SCHEMA-V1), PART REAL, and the point with the widest blast radius either way. kaay is taught by MR-C02-kaay (chapter 9, schema-v1, no atom). kon and kitii appear nowhere at all -- who and how-many being two of the things a wh-item paper asks most.

points.label: the exclamative kitii with an adjective or adverb
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: a pronoun before a postposition takes its oblique form
points.note: Untaught, and blocked behind MR-A1-N-09. Spanish's stressed pronouns after a preposition are the same demand with a much smaller cost.

points.label: the tuu / tumhii politeness contrast, and which to use with a stranger
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC: Spanish's tu/usted is not an A1 point in the source, but Marathi's speaking paper is an interview with an unmet interlocutor and rubric dimension 2 scores the choice. SCHEMA-V1 MEASUREMENT GAP, ENTIRELY: MR-C02-tu-tumhi teaches exactly this contrast and declares no atom.

points.label: place deictics: ithe, tithe
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: time deictics: aataa, aaj, udyaa, kaal
points.note: udyaa appears inside two fixed farewells -- MR-C04-udya-bhetu (schema-v1) and MR-A1-MESSAGE-LINE-SEE-TOMORROW -- and never as a time word a learner could reuse. aataa, aaj and kaal do not appear at all.

points.label: quantity adverbs: khuup, jaraa
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: manner adverbs: baraM and its opposite
connective adverbs: sudhaa and its negative counterpart
points.note: Closed by MR-C36-sudhaa (chapter 36). The negative counterpart is not a second word: sudhaa in a negated sentence reads 'not even', and the lesson teaches both readings of the one word.

points.label: interrogative adverbs: kuthe, kadhii, kasaa
points.note: PART MEASUREMENT GAP (SCHEMA-V1), PART REAL. The agreeing kasaa/kashii/kasaM is taught by MR-C03-kasa (chapter 10, schema-v1, no atom); kuthe and kadhii appear nowhere. SPINE-ASK-LOCATION is an A1 core node and the track omits its only concept, QUESTION-WHERE.

points.label: kaa against kaaran: asking why, and answering it
points.note: Closed by MR-C34-kaa-why and MR-C34-kaaran (chapter 34). Both halves are required, which is what the point asks for: asking why and answering it.

points.label: the present habitual: the regular paradigm, all persons
points.note: Only the 1SG masculine and feminine forms carry atoms (MR-PHRASE-YETO-YETE-01, MR-GRAMMAR-PRESENT-GENDER). One 2PL copula form, aahaat, sits inside schema-v1 MR-C03-tumhi-kase-aahat. A candidate can say what HE does and nothing about anyone else.

points.label: the copula aahe, and the fact that a Marathi clause ends on it
the high-frequency motion verbs yene and jaane
the present continuous in -t aahe
points.note: Untaught. 'What are you doing?' is an A1 interview question.

points.label: the past habitual
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the simple past, and its agreement with the object
points.note: Untaught. The A1 listening paper's third part is 'a personal account', which is past-tense by genre.

points.label: the ergative -ne on the subject of a past transitive verb
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC, with no Spanish counterpart because Spanish has no ergative alignment. It is not a refinement of the past tense but the GATE on it: a Marathi past transitive clause without it is ungrammatical, so MR-A1-V-06 cannot be closed independently of this point.

points.label: the perfect
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: irregular past stems: gelaa, khaallaa, kelaa
points.note: Untaught, and the three commonest verbs in the language are among them.

points.label: the imperative, plain and polite
points.note: EMPTY-INTRODUCES MEASUREMENT GAP. The polite imperative is drilled outright: MR-R22-request-verbs (chapter 26) is built on dyaa, pyaa, aannaa and thevaa, and MR-R23-wellbeing-verbs adds basaa. Both are schema-v2 with `introduces: []` and both practise the INFINITIVE atoms, so five taught imperative forms carry no atom between them. ghyaa is taught too, in schema-v1 MR-C04-kalji-ghya. The form is in the book and invisible to the measurement.

points.label: the -ne infinitive as a non-finite form
the conjunctive participle in -uun, which links two actions
points.note: bhetuun occurs inside the fixed line MR-A1-MESSAGE-LINE-MEETING and the form is never stated. Spanish's gerund is the nearest thing it has; the Marathi form does more work and is taught less.

points.label: the past participle used adjectivally
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the present tense declares the speaker's own gender
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC. Spanish verbs never mark the speaker's gender, so no Spanish point covers this; assessment-spec.md makes it assessable by requiring consistent agreement rather than one assumed candidate identity.

points.label: dative-subject verbs, where the person is never the subject
compound verbs formed with karne
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC: a large share of the everyday verb stock is noun-plus-karne, a pattern Spanish has no productive equivalent of at A1.

points.label: the future
points.note: PART MEASUREMENT GAP (EMPTY-INTRODUCES), PART REAL. bhetuu is taught three times over -- MR-C04-bhetu, -punha-bhetu, -udya-bhetu, all schema-v1 -- and chaalel, a third-person future, is drilled by MR-R23-wellbeing-verbs (schema-v2, `introduces: []`, practising the SENSE atom rather than the form). Always a fixed phrase, never a tense a learner could build.

points.label: ability: -uu shakne, and yene with a language
points.note: Only the frozen line 'malaa maraathii yete' exists (MR-A1-MESSAGE-LINE-KNOW-MARATHI). SPINE-SAY-WHAT-I-HAVE-AND-CAN-DO omits both VERB-HAVE and VERB-CAN.

points.label: wanting and needing: paahije, havaa, nako
points.note: Still untaught as a set. nako now has an atom (MR-LEX-NAKO, chapter 32) and closes the REFUSAL points on its own, but paahije and havaa -- the wanting and needing halves this point names, and the ones the transactional role-play is built on -- have no exponent. One of three is not this point.

points.label: possession: the postposition plus aahe construction
points.note: Untaught. Marathi has no verb 'to have', so this is blocked behind MR-A1-N-09 and the postpositions rather than behind a missing word.

points.label: the locative -t and -var: in, at, on
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC (Spanish uses prepositions and needs no stem). Untaught, and it is what the reading paper's signs and notices are made of.

points.label: accompaniment and instrument: -shii, barobar, -ne
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC. 'With my friend' is an A1 sentence and the track teaches mitra with no way to attach it.

points.label: source and starting point: -huun, paasuun
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC. 'I am from Pune' is the second sentence of every A1 speaking interview.

points.label: goal and limit: -kade, paryant
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC. Required by the transactional role-play.

points.label: postpositions of place: var, khaalii, madhye, javal, samor
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC in form; the demand is Spanish's relative-position point. SPINE-ASK-LOCATION is an A1 node the track does not realize.

points.label: noun-phrase complements: an adjective, a genitive phrase, a relative clause
points.note: Only the genitive is taught (MR-A1-POS-03); the other two are blocked behind MR-A1-ADJ-01 and MR-A1-PRON-05.

points.label: subject-verb agreement as a stated rule
the vocative: addressing someone by name
degree modifiers: khuup, jaraa, puresaa
points.note: Untaught, and blocked behind MR-A1-ADJ-01: there is nothing yet to modify.

points.label: the liking verb and its argument structure
one copula where Spanish has two
the attribute and its agreement
points.note: Blocked behind MR-A1-ADJ-01.

points.label: the direct object: animates take -laa, inanimates do not
points.note: Untaught. Spanish's personal a is the same distinction under a different marker, which makes this one of the clearest one-to-one transfers in the file.

points.label: the indirect object
points.note: The dative MARKER is taught (MR-A1-P-01) but only on an experiencer. Giving something to somebody is a different frame and no lesson supplies it.

points.label: subject-object-verb order, and where a circumstantial goes
declaratives, affirmative and negative
points.note: Closed by MR-C32-nahi-verb (chapter 32), which realizes VERB-NEGATE on SPINE-NEGATE-AND-ASK. Affirmative declaratives were already taught; only the negation was missing, so one atom closes the point.

points.label: yes-or-no questions, with kaa and with intonation
points.note: Closed by MR-C33-kaa-polar (chapter 33), which realizes QUESTION-POLAR. Both atoms are required because the point names both routes, and a listening paper supplies the rise without the particle.

points.label: questions with an asking word
points.note: SCHEMA-V1 MEASUREMENT GAP. Two complete wh-questions are taught as whole phrases -- MR-C02-tumche-naav-kaay-aahe and MR-C03-tumhi-kase-aahat, both schema-v1 -- so the word order has been SHOWN twice and never stated, and neither can be probed. Kept separate from MR-A1-PRON-06 because knowing the question word is not knowing where to put it.

points.label: existential sentences
points.note: Untaught. Spanish's impersonal hay is Marathi's aahe with a locative, so this is blocked behind MR-A1-P-02.

points.label: transitive and intransitive sentences
points.note: Both types are demonstrated in taught lines; the distinction is never stated, and in Marathi it is not a grammarian's nicety -- it decides whether the past tense takes the ergative (MR-A1-V-07).

points.label: joining with aani
points.note: Closed by MR-C30-aani (chapter 30), which teaches aani joining two full clauses, not only two nouns -- the 30-40 connected words of the writing task want the clause join.

points.label: negative coordination: naa ... naa
points.note: Closed by MR-C31-naa-naa (chapter 31). The doubled naa is taught as a shape that must be said twice; saying it once is explicitly named as an unfinished sentence.

points.label: disjunctive coordination: kinvaa
points.note: Closed by MR-C30-kinva (chapter 30).

points.label: adversative coordination: pan
points.note: Closed by MR-C30-pan (chapter 30). Its example contradicts with the already-taught existential naahii, so the lesson needs no forward reference to sentence negation, which arrives two chapters later.

points.label: distributive coordination: ek ... dusraa
points.note: Closed by MR-C31-dusra (chapter 31). Both halves are required: ek was already taught in the numbers chapter, dusraa is new, and the point is the frame rather than either word.

points.label: the verbal noun as direct object
points.note: Untaught. Blocked behind MR-A1-V-19: the verbs that take one are the wanting verbs.

points.label: a finite clause as object, with the thinking verb
points.note: Closed by MR-C35-kii (chapter 35). Both atoms are required because the point is the thinking verb WITH a clause attached, not the complementizer in the abstract.

points.label: the correlative relative clause
points.note: Still untaught. MR-C36-jevha (chapter 36) teaches the jevhaa/tevhaa correlative and NAMES the ja-/ta- stems that jo/to share, but naming a shape is not teaching the relative clause, and the point is not scored as covered on that.

points.label: causal clauses with kaaran
points.note: Closed by MR-C34-kaaran (chapter 34), which also realizes CONNECTIVE-BECAUSE on SPINE-SAY-WHY; that node's omission ledger is now empty.

points.label: purpose with -saathii plus the verbal noun
points.note: Closed by MR-C35-saathi (chapter 35). The lesson teaches the -ne -> -nyaasaathii swap as one productive rule and says in as many words that the general oblique-stem rule behind the -nyaa- (MR-A1-N-09) is still owed.

points.label: simultaneity: jevhaa and the -lyaavar participle
points.note: Closed by MR-C36-jevha and MR-C36-lyaavar (chapter 36). Both atoms are required because the point names both exponents, and they mean different things: jevhaa is simultaneity, -lyaavar is sequence.

points.label: identify oneself or another by name
ask for information about a person, a thing or a place
points.note: SCHEMA-V1 MEASUREMENT GAP, PARTLY. 'tumchaM naav kaay aahe?' is taught outright by MR-C02-tumche-naav-kaay-aahe (chapter 9, no atom). Asking about a THING or a PLACE needs kuthe, which appears nowhere.

points.label: give personal information: name, age, origin
points.note: One third of it works. Name is taught and so is city as a form field; AGE needs a number above five (MR-A1-QU-03) and ORIGIN needs the ablative (MR-A1-P-04). This is the A1 speaking interview's opening question.

points.label: ask for confirmation with a tag
points.note: Closed by MR-C31-naa-tag (chapter 31), exactly as this note predicted: one syllable.

points.label: confirm or deny the previous statement
ask for an opinion by handing the turn back
points.note: Untaught, and it is what a role-play turn is made of.

points.label: give an opinion with malaa vaatta
ask for an evaluation
points.note: Blocked behind MR-A1-ADV-07: the question word kasaa is schema-v1 only.

points.label: express approval and disapproval
points.note: Closed once sentence negation existed. Approval runs through the already-taught chaalel; disapproval is MR-C32-nahi-verb's own worked example, malaa duudh aavaDat naahii.

points.label: express disagreement
points.note: Still untaught, and the shape of the remainder is now clearer. Sentence negation exists (MR-GRAMMAR-NEGATE-NAHI) and pan can contradict a clause, but neither is the DISCOURSE move of contradicting something an interlocutor just said, and no lesson supplies it. Deliberately not claimed on the strength of the two nearby exponents.

points.label: show scepticism: malaa maahiit naahii
points.note: Closed by MR-C32-nahi-verb (chapter 32), which teaches malaa maahiit naahii as a named construction rather than leaving the two halves to be assembled.

points.label: express possibility
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: ask whether somebody knows something
points.note: Closed by MR-C33-kaa-polar (chapter 33), whose worked example IS this move: maahiit aahe kaa?

points.label: ask about ability to do something
points.note: Still blocked. MR-A1-OS-02 is now closed, so the question half exists; the ability half does not, because MR-A1-V-18 (-uu shakne) remains untaught. Half a pair buys nothing and this is not scored as covered.

points.label: ask about a preference by offering alternatives
points.note: Blocked behind MR-A1-CO-03: offering alternatives needs 'or'.

points.label: express wishes
points.note: Untaught; SPINE-SAY-WHAT-I-WANT omits VERB-WANT.

points.label: ask about plans and intentions
points.note: Blocked behind the future (MR-A1-V-17) and the polar question.

points.label: express plans and intentions
points.note: Blocked behind the future.

points.label: give an order or an instruction
points.note: EMPTY-INTRODUCES MEASUREMENT GAP -- see MR-A1-V-10. Five polite imperatives are drilled by lessons that declare no atoms. Public notices, which the reading paper's second part is made of, are written in exactly this form.

points.label: respond to an order, a request or a plea
grant permission
points.note: Closed by MR-C33-kaa-polar (chapter 33): chaalel kaa? asks, and the already-taught chaalel grants.

points.label: refuse permission
points.note: Closed by MR-C32-nako (chapter 32), exactly as this note predicted.

points.label: offer and invite
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: accept a proposal, an offer or an invitation
points.note: The acceptance TOKENS exist (ho, chaalel); there is no invitation vocabulary for them to accept, so the exchange cannot be completed and the point is not scored as covered on the strength of half of it.

points.label: decline a proposal, an offer or an invitation
points.note: Closed by MR-C32-nako (chapter 32). The softener this note asked for is the already-taught dhanyavaad, and the lesson teaches the whole decline as one line -- nako, dhanyavaad -- rather than leaving the learner to join them.

points.label: choose a greeting that fits the time of day
points.note: SPINE-TIME-OF-DAY is an A1 core node and the track omits all four of its greeting concepts along with its four time words.

points.label: ask somebody else's name
points.note: SCHEMA-V1 MEASUREMENT GAP, ENTIRELY. MR-C02-tumche-naav-kaay-aahe (chapter 9) teaches it outright, declares no atom, and is invisible to every probe. With MR-A1-F5-08 it is one of the two clearest cases in this file of the corpus being better than its own measurement says.

points.label: apologise
points.note: The RESPONSE to an apology is taught -- 'kaahii harkat naahii', MR-C03-kaahi-harkat-nahi, schema-v1 -- and the apology itself is not, in either schema: maaf karaa and kshamaa karaa appear nowhere. A candidate who can only forgive and never apologise is the wrong half of SPINE-POLITE-REQUEST-REPAIR.

points.label: ask how somebody is, and answer
points.note: SCHEMA-V1 MEASUREMENT GAP, ENTIRELY. Both halves are taught in chapter 10 -- MR-C03-tumhi-kase-aahat gives the question, MR-C03-mi-bara-aahe the answer -- and both are schema-v1. The v2 material under SPINE-CHECK-WELLBEING is lexical, so the probe sees vocabulary arranged around an exchange it cannot see.

points.label: offer condolences
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: congratulate, and mark a festival
points.note: Untaught. Spanish separates the toast from the congratulation; Marathi's festival greetings carry both and are merged here into one point.

points.label: open a conversation and react to its opening
ask for a person and respond
points.note: Untaught; blocked behind MR-A1-PRON-06 and MR-A1-OS-03.

points.label: show that one is following what is said
ask somebody to repeat, slow down or be quiet
points.note: Untaught, and assessment-spec.md gives it teeth: the A1 speaking interlocutor 'may repeat once slowly', which a candidate has to be able to ASK for.

points.label: existence and non-existence
points.note: Still blocked, and now by one thing rather than two. MR-A1-OS-01 is closed, so non-existence can be said; existence in a place still needs MR-A1-V-20 and the locative MR-A1-P-02.

points.label: presence and absence
points.note: Blocked behind the locative, MR-A1-P-02.

points.label: stating a general quality
points.note: Blocked behind MR-A1-ADJ-01.

points.label: locating an event in time
points.note: Untaught; needs the clock and the calendar, neither of which exists.

points.label: certainty and uncertainty
points.note: Closed by MR-C35-kii (chapter 35). The uncertain half this note said had no exponent is malaa vaaTta kii ... -- hedging an assertion by putting it under the seeming verb. The certain half remains plain assertion (MR-A1-F2-09).

points.label: measures: size, distance and weight
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: location: being somewhere
points.note: Blocked behind MR-A1-P-02 and MR-A1-ADV-01.

points.label: relative position: javal, laamb, ujvii, daavii
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: distance
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: orientation and direction
points.note: Untaught; blocked behind MR-A1-P-05.

points.label: order: first, next, before and after
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: origin: where one is from
points.note: The city is taught as a form FIELD (MR-A1-FORM-LABEL-SHAHAR); saying one comes FROM it needs the ablative of MR-A1-P-04. The noun without the postposition answers a form and not an interviewer.

points.label: the clock, and the parts of the day
points.note: SPINE-TIME-OF-DAY is an A1 core node with NO realization at all: all nine concepts omitted. The listening paper's announcements are about times.

points.label: today, yesterday, tomorrow
points.note: udyaa occurs only inside fixed farewells; aaj and kaal do not occur.

points.label: the days of the week
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the months, and writing a date
points.note: Untaught; the A1 practical form asks for one.

points.label: the seasons
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: before and after: ordering two events
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: hearing
points.note: The ORGAN is taught (MR-LEX-KAAN) and the verb is not: SPINE-SAY-WHAT-I-DO omits VERB-HEAR. There is an eighteen-minute listening paper, so this is not a decorative gap.

points.label: colour
points.note: Untaught. Colours are the standard A1 descriptor set and what a sign-and-label item uses for its distractors.

points.label: age
points.note: Untaught, and blocked behind MR-A1-QU-03: saying an age needs a number above five.

points.label: accessibility: open and closed, the way in and the way out
points.note: Untaught. SPINE-NAME-EVERYDAY-ACTIONS omits VERB-OPEN and VERB-CLOSE, and these four words are most of what a sign set says.

points.label: general evaluation: good, bad, all right
value and price
points.note: Untaught, and it is the content of the speaking paper's third part. Blocked jointly by MR-A1-QU-03 and MR-A1-V-19.

points.label: attractiveness
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: quality: calling a thing good or bad
points.note: Blocked behind MR-A1-ADJ-01; baraM evaluates a state, not a thing.

points.label: ease and difficulty
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: physical characteristics
points.note: Untaught; blocked behind MR-A1-ADJ-01. The A1 speaking paper asks for a one-minute description of a familiar person.

points.label: actions and positions of the body
character and personality
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: personal data: name, address, telephone, age
points.note: Name and city are taught as form fields; address, telephone and age are not, and the telephone number additionally needs the Devanagari digits of MR-A1-OR-24. This is the A1 writing paper's first task.

points.label: documents: an identity card or a passport
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: personal objects
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the immediate family: mother, father, son, daughter, husband, wife
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC SPLIT of the Spanish family point, because the shape of the gap is the finding: siblings and 'family' are taught and not one PARENT is. 'Tell me about your family' is the standard A1 interview opener and it cannot currently be answered.

points.label: celebrations and family, social and religious occasions
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the meals of the day
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: foodstuffs
points.note: One foodstuff is taught, bhaakarii, and one word is not a domain: no item asking a candidate to pick a food from three options can be built out of it.

points.label: dishes and courses
points.note: Untaught: bhaat, bhaajii, polii and jevan have no atoms.

points.label: eating out
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: educational institutions
points.note: Untaught; shaalaa has no atom.

points.label: teachers and students
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the school day: timetable and term
points.note: Untaught; blocked behind the clock and the calendar.

points.label: examinations and marks
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: classroom language
points.note: Untaught. assessment-spec.md allows A1 directions in a declared support language, so this is a real but softened demand at this rung; from A2 the directions are in Marathi.

points.label: teaching materials and classroom objects
points.note: Untaught; pustak and pen have no atoms.

points.label: professions and posts
points.note: Untaught, and it is a field on the A1 practical form.

points.label: workplaces and tools
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: working activity
points.note: SCHEMA-V1 MEASUREMENT GAP. kaam karne is taught by MR-C05-kaam-karne (chapter 12) and raahne by MR-C05-rahne, both schema-v1 with no atoms, so 'I work' and 'I live' are reachable and invisible.

points.label: looking for work
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: conditions, rights and obligations at work
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: describing a worker
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: free time and what one likes doing in it
shows and outings
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: sport
points.note: Untaught; SPINE-SAY-WHAT-I-DO omits VERB-PLAY and VERB-RUN.

points.label: games
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the media
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: written correspondence: the lines of a short personal message
the telephone
points.note: Untaught, and giving a number needs the Devanagari digits of MR-A1-OR-24.

points.label: the printed press
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: television and radio
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the internet, and giving an e-mail address
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: renting, buying and moving
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: types of dwelling and its rooms
points.note: SPINE-NAME-EVERYDAY-THINGS is an A1 core node and the track omits LODGING-ROOM, its only listed concept.

points.label: domestic activities
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: household objects and furniture
points.note: Untaught; daar and khidkii have no atoms, and a sign-and-label reading part labels exactly this kind of thing.

points.label: the post office
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: banks and money services
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: health services
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: police and emergency services
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: shops, shopkeepers and shopping
points.note: Untaught. dukaan has no atom, and the A1 speaking paper's third part is a transactional role-play.

points.label: clothing and footwear
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: paying
points.note: Untaught; paise has no atom and the numbers stop at five.

points.label: health and illness: saying how one feels
the clinic and the hospital
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: medicine
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: hygiene and daily routine
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: travel documents and luggage
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: accommodation
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: getting about: bus, train, ticket, station
points.note: Untaught; SPINE-HANDLE-TRAVEL has no realization in this track.

points.label: money
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: buyer and seller
points.note: Untaught; SPINE-NAME-EVERYDAY-ACTIONS omits VERB-BUY.

points.label: businesses and organisations
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: industry and energy
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: computers and everyday technology
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the state and its institutions
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: law and rules
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the arts as a field
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: music and dance
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: building, sculpture and painting
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: literature and reading
points.note: Untaught as a domain. vaachne is taught as an ACTION (MR-A1-NE06-04) and no noun names a book, a poem or a film. Spanish's photography and cinema points are merged in here rather than split, since at A1 they are one thin field.

points.label: religion and belief
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the sky and the natural world at large
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: town and countryside
points.note: Untaught; rastaa and gaav have no atoms.

points.label: weather and climate
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: animals
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: plants and trees
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: the akshara principle: a consonant letter carries an inherent a, and a matra replaces it
the shirorekha headline, which binds the letters of one written word
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC: the Latin alphabet has no equivalent, and it is what makes a Devanagari word one visual unit.

points.label: the velar row ka kha ga gha
the palatal row ca cha ja jha
the retroflex row tta ttha dda ddha nna
points.note: Four fifths taught -- MR-SCRIPT-TTA-01, -TTHA-01, -DDA-01 and -NNA-01 -- and the fifth missing: no atom introduces DDHA. A row a reader can only rebuild four ways is not a row, and DDHA is not rare (dhag, gadhav, vaadh).

points.label: the dental row ta tha da dha na
points.note: TA, DA, DHA and NA are taught; THA, the aspirated dental, has no atom. It spells thodaa and the ordinal-forming -thaa, so the gap sits inside A1 vocabulary rather than beyond it.

points.label: the labial row pa pha ba bha ma
points.note: PA, BA, BHA and MA are taught; PHA has no atom. Without it a candidate cannot read phon, phal or the very common phakta.

points.label: the semivowels ya ra la va
the three sibilants sha ssa sa, and ha
the nasals of the velar and palatal rows, which survive mainly inside conjuncts
points.note: Untaught. Lower priority than the other rows and listed because the row inventory is not closed without them.

points.label: Marathi's retroflex lla, the letter Hindi does not have
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC, and the single glyph that most clearly marks a text as Marathi rather than Hindi.

points.label: the independent vowel letters, used word-initially
points.note: A, AA, U, UU and E are taught as independents. I, II, O, AI and AU are not, so a candidate cannot begin a word with them -- and the reading genres are full of such words (ithe, ekun, aai, olakh).

points.label: the vowel signs aa i ii u uu e o
the ai and au vowel signs
points.note: Neither has an atom. They spell aai (mother), paise (money) and kaay (what) -- three items this inventory separately marks as untaught vocabulary, so the debts compound.

points.label: the vocalic r sign, read ru in Marathi
the i-matra is written BEFORE the letter it is read after
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC decoding rule with no Latin counterpart: the reading order and the writing order come apart, which is the commonest early decoding error.

points.label: anusvara and candrabindu: the two nasal marks and the difference between them
visarga, in the tatsama words a printed text keeps it in
virama, and the principle that two consonants join when the inherent vowel goes
the frequent conjuncts themselves: kssa, jnya, tra, shra
points.note: The PRINCIPLE is taught (MR-SCRIPT-VIRAMA-01) and no individual conjunct is. Spanish's digraph point is the nearest analogue and is far cheaper: Spanish has five digraphs, Marathi has a productive system.

points.label: the r-forms: reph above the line and rakaar below it
points.note: Untaught, and they do not look like a virama join at all, so the conjunct principle does not transfer to them by itself. They appear in karya, purna and the reph of maarg.

points.label: spelling a word from its sound: syllable division and the doubled consonant
reading a whole word back from its pieces
the Devanagari digits zero to nine
points.note: No atom introduces a single digit. The A1 writing paper is 'complete a practical form', and a form asks for a phone number, a house number and a date. This is the cheapest large gap in the file: ten glyphs, and they unlock an entire paper part.

points.label: the danda, and the full stop that has largely replaced it
points.note: Every headword in the corpus punctuates with a full stop. A candidate who has never seen a danda meets it on the first authentic notice.

points.label: the comma
points.note: Closed by MR-W34-comma (chapter 34), which teaches both jobs the writing task needs: the list comma that stands in for aani, and the comma after a named reader.

points.label: the colon, as a form label uses it
question and exclamation marks
points.note: Closed by MR-W33-question-mark (chapter 33). Both marks are required because the point names both, and the lesson states the rule they share: one mark, at the end, with nothing opening the sentence.

points.label: the remaining marks a printed text uses: brackets, quotation marks, the hyphen and the dash
points.note: Untaught. Merged from five Spanish points because at A1 the demand is recognition rather than production, and recognising them is one skill.

points.label: abbreviations a form or a notice uses, and how they are written
points.note: Untaught. Spanish's superscript abbreviation letters are merged in here: the demand behind both is reading a shortened word on a form, and Marathi shortens with a full stop rather than a raised letter.

points.label: initialisms and acronyms
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: symbols: the rupee sign, the numeral sign, the percent sign
points.note: Untaught, and a price on a sign is written with one.

points.label: the two pronunciations of ca and ja: palatal, and the dental ts/dz Marathi keeps
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC. The Spanish inventory deliberately enumerates no pronunciation points at all -- its source publishes no A1/A2 split for them -- so this whole category is derived from the assessed variety in assessment-spec.md and from the listening envelope, not from the proxy.

points.label: the four-way stop contrast: voicing crossed with aspiration, in every row
the dental/retroflex place contrast: ta-tta, da-dda, na-nna, la-lla
nasalization: what the anusvara does to a following stop, and what candrabindu does to a vowel
reading the formal register a public notice uses: the Sanskrit spelling of a word speech has worn down
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC. Public notices -- the reading paper's second part -- are written in a heavily tatsama register, so recognising the formal twin of an everyday word is a reading demand and not a piece of philology.

points.label: hearing a borrowed doublet as the same word as its everyday twin
word-final inherent-vowel deletion: when the written a is not said
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC and untaught. Nothing states the rule, and it governs how nearly every taught word is pronounced -- naav, not naava. A learner who reads the akshara principle literally mispronounces the whole vocabulary, which the listening and speaking papers both score.

points.label: word stress and the rhythm of a short phrase
points.note: MARATHI-SPECIFIC and untaught. The listening envelope specifies 90-110 wpm at A1, so rhythm is assessed whether or not it is taught.
